Earn 9% Returns Every Six Months in Tazewell County Tax Lien Sale!

Click Here to Get Dustin Hahn’s Tax Lien and Deed FREE Mini-Course

Looking to earn solid returns on your investments? Check out the Tazewell County Tax Lien Sale for a chance to earn 9% every six months!

Tazewell County, Illinois, holds its Annual Tax Lien Sale every October. During this sale, you can buy tax lien certificates and start making up to 9% return every six months for up to 3 years. These sales happen because when property taxes remain unpaid, the county eventually puts the liens up for auction, where investors can bid on the interest rate of the lien certificates.

With a population of around 130,000, Tazewell County blends history and modern economy, presenting an untapped real estate opportunity. The winning bidder’s interest rate, capped at 9%, applies every six months, potentially accumulating up to a maximum of 54% return during the redemption period.

After the sale, homeowners in Tazewell County have a two-and-a-half to three-year redemption period. If the property is not redeemed, the buyer can petition the court for a tax deed to take ownership. For investors, Tazewell County’s tax sales offer opportunities for high returns or strategic potential property ownership.

Pro Tips

  • Prepare Funds: Ensure you have the necessary funds ready for the registration fee and any winning bids.
  • Do Your Research: Investigate the properties beforehand to assess their value and potential for return.
  • Understand the Redemption Period: Be aware of the timelines and procedures for property redemption and acquiring tax deeds.

FAQs

Q: What happens if the property owner redeems the lien?

A: If the property owner redeems the lien, you will receive your initial investment back plus the accrued interest.

Q: Can I inspect the properties before bidding?

A: Yes, it’s advisable to do thorough research or inspection to assess the property’s condition and value.

Q: What if the property is not redeemed? A: If the property is not redeemed within the specified period, you can petition the court for a tax deed to take ownership of the property.
